newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila bank sub-index drops 1.1 pct in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Manila bank sub-index drops 1.1 pct in late trade.

text.p: The Philippine Stock Exchange's banks and financial services sub-index fell 11.66 points, or 1.1 percent, to 1,044.79 points in late trading on Monday on fears that a fall in property prices could affect banks, brokers said.

Actively traded banking issues that posted losses in late trade on Monday included Metropolitan Bank & Trust Co (Metrobank) which was down 15 pesos to 630 and Equitable Banking Corp which fell two pesos to 114. Philippine National Bank also lost 2.5 pesos to 270.

"We were hit by the Thai virus. I think mainly the downturn in the property sector is linked to the banking sector as what had happened in Thailand," said Saturnino Mejia, research head at Guoco Securities.
"Investors are probably comparing us to the Thai market that is suffering a similar problem," said Cilette Liboro, research head at Citisecurities Inc.
The Thailand property sector is reeling under a four-year slump with an oversupply problem.
Mejia said latest data from the Central Bank showed that average loan exposure of local banks to the property sector is about 10 to 11 percent.
Audi Pantillano, analyst at Angping & Associates Securities, said selling on banking issues had begun some three weeks ago triggered by cash-strapped Victorias Milling Corp's bid for debt moratorium.
